stage1.impression: A night street view through a shopfront: EARF frosted on the glass, a big pale lightbox with a blurred dancer on the left, and a deep warm room fading off to the right. The mood is plausible, but the whole frame is one muddy sepia. The glass has no street reflections, so it reads as a hole rather than a pane. The mullions are smooth brown tubes, and at 1:1 the interior is soft and blotchy. Worst of all, I can't find a hero object: the only saturated colour is two red slivers peeking out behind dark lounge chairs.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker reads at a glance through the clear pane: its full silhouette is visible, no chair cuts across it, and its red glow and spill are the clear colour accent (red region r_median > 110 with r-g > 50)
The shopfront glass reads as glass: faint, clean reflections of the street and kerb lamps across the panes, with the interior still readable behind them
The blackened steel mullions and header read near black with an uneven brownish sheen and crisp edges, not as smooth mid-brown cylinders
The frosted EARF reads as acid-etched glass (soft, slightly translucent, light falling off across it), not a flat opaque vinyl sticker
The grade separates neutral materials from the warm light: concrete and steel read greyish while the lamps stay warm, not the whole frame in one brown wash (frame r/b median ratio currently 2.0)
Interior detail at full resolution with no denoiser smear: fir beams, the record wall and the floor show texture, not mush

defects.what: The Ember speaker is hidden behind a lounge chair; only a red sliver and some red spill show
Second red sliver and its floor reflection, also occluded by chairs; reads as a stray red light, not a speaker
Frame lum_median 20.5, just under the 22 floor; 78 % of pixels below 40
Monochrome sepia grade (r 28 / g 19 / b 14 median): no neutral surface anywhere, so the speaker's colour has nothing to read against
No reflections on the shopfront glass at all; the street lamps and the street behind the camera never appear, so the panes read as missing
Left mullion reads as a smooth mid-brown pipe (median 32), not blackened steel
Centre mullion is the same: smooth, light, rounded-looking, no patina, no sharp arris
EARF lettering is flat and uniform (median 74, little variation), opaque and pinkish; reads as a vinyl sticker
The lightbox is a large flat low-contrast slab (range 73) that takes the left fifth of the frame and pulls the eye away from the room
Bell shade clipped to a white rectangle with no form
Small clipped white squares on the chairs and table read like phone screens or LEDs, not lamps
Ceiling and beams are low contrast (lum_range 28) and soft, with denoiser blotching; the haze turns the back of the room to mud rather than atmosphere
The concrete fascia over the shopfront is the only real texture in the frame, and it is cut off at the top edge

changes.problem: The hero, the Ember speaker at the far end, is hidden behind the lounge chairs, so the frame has no subject.

evidence.measured: Red pixels only in slivers about 15 px wide at x 455-470 and 575-590; the chair silhouettes at x 470-610 cover the cabinets

change.to: move the camera sideways in y (try 1.6 to 2.0) and raise it to z 1.7 so the line of sight to one Ember passes between the chairs, then re-aim so that speaker sits in the right-hand clear pane on the right third line; lens 40-50 mm so the speaker is at least 60 px tall in the 720 px proof. Keep the verticals level

changes.expected: One Ember cabinet fully visible from base to horn through clear glass, with no chair overlapping it, and the red read at once as an object

changes.problem: Even where it shows, the Ember is too weak to be the frame's one colour; it reads as a stray red bulb.

evidence.measured: r_median 62, g 31.5, b 24: dull brick, barely brighter than the surrounding brown room

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area
change.to: 160-200 W/m2 at 2700 K, aimed so it lights through the cabinet from behind and the side and puts a soft red spill on the floor and wall around it

changes.expected: The speaker's tint glows through the acrylic with the white batts visible; it is the single saturated object in the frame

changes.problem: The shopfront glass shows no reflections, so it reads as an empty opening and gives up the street-at-night story.

evidence.measured: Upper interior is uniform dark (median 15.8, range 28) with no trace of the street lamps or a facade across the road

change.from: 3 x point 120 W, nothing behind the camera for the glass to reflect
change.to: put a dim facade plane behind and above the camera (lit windows, emission about 0.05-0.1, cool-neutral 3500-4000 K) and move one street lamp into the reflected view, so the glass picks up a faint, clean reflection across its upper third

changes.expected: A faint ghost of street lamps and a lit window over the top third of the glass, the interior still readable through it

changes.problem: The frame sits just under the brightness floor, and a single brown wash flattens every material.

change.to: exposure 3.8, white_balance_k 2700 (neutralise toward the lamps so concrete and steel go greyish while the 2400 K pendants still read warm)

changes.expected: Frame median about 25-30; neutral surfaces read near grey (b_median at least 0.65 of r_median); the lamps stay amber

changes.problem: The mullions read as smooth mid-brown tubes, not blackened steel.

evidence.measured: lum_median 27.9, p95 57.6, smooth gradient across the width with no sharp edge

change.to: base colour about #1a1714, roughness 0.35-0.6 varied with a mottled patina map, slight brown oxide at the edges, a hard 1 mm arris that catches one thin highlight from the street lamp

changes.expected: Near-black flat bars with a crisp edge highlight and an uneven sheen

changes.problem: The frosted name reads as an opaque flat pink sticker, not etched glass.

evidence.measured: lum_median 74 with little variation inside the letters; r/b 93/59 tinted pink

change.setting: the window's frosted name (emission) and frosted acrylic roughness
change.to: emission 0.004-0.006 with a light transmission term (roughness about 0.5) so the room's lights blur through the letters, and the street lamp's light falling off left to right across them

changes.expected: Soft, slightly translucent letters that show blurred interior light through them, about 15-20 % less bright and no longer pink

changes.problem: Bell and the small table lights clip to white rectangles with no form, which reads as CG or as phone screens.

evidence.measured: clip_pct 1.2, p95 201; the shade is a flat white block

change.from: Bell none (the shade's emission blows out)
change.to: lower the shade's emission about 40 % and add a small 2-4 W, 2400 K point inside each Bell, so the shade grades from a bright core to a warm rim and casts a pool on the table

changes.expected: Lamps bright but not blown, each with a visible warm pool on its table

changes.problem: The haze and low contrast turn the back of the room to mud and hide the fir and the record wall.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 23.5 across the record wall: blacks lifted by the haze, detail smeared

change.setting: haze in the room's air / record-wall strip
change.to: density 0.003, record-wall strip 1.5 with its spots at 12 W, so the shelves and spines read and the blacks between the pools return

changes.expected: Deeper blacks between the pools, the record spines legible, and atmosphere only in the light cones

out_of_scope.request: Move the lounge chairs in the listening room so they stop hiding the Ember pair
out_of_scope.why: The room's layout is fixed by the card; c1 solves this with the camera instead

out_of_scope.request: Make the lightbox panel smaller or move it so it stops taking the left fifth of the frame
out_of_scope.why: The screens and the shopfront are part of the fixed room design; only their brightness may change. Reframing in c1 can reduce how much of it is in frame
